text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition tells you almost nothing here. Both you and the successful candidate are women, so sex can't plausibly explain why she was preferred over you. An all-woman panel is unusual in finance, but unusual isn't evidence — and raising it would invite the obvious reply that they selected a woman.

Your real grievances are stronger: a two-week silence on a reasonable request, and a vague criterion ("broad experience of regulatory affairs") that may not have appeared in the advertised specification. Chase the written explanation, ask which criteria were scored and how, and request the scoring matrix. If the job spec emphasised quantitative modelling, a mismatch between advertised and applied criteria is your argument.
